split_rationale: Configuration ACs join configuration-settings data with construction lifecycle. Containment ACs join repository-root/target data with runtime lifecycle. The resource/storage preservation AC shares neither the same data nor a second signal kind and therefore remains a singleton. These are draft delivery proposals only; the singleton is best evaluated as a preservation verification subtask rather than evidence of a new resource subsystem.

candidate_subtasks.title: Layered configuration snapshot construction
candidate_subtasks.description: Build the operation settings snapshot from user defaults and root-to-leaf repository/local configuration. Own effective-directory and Git-root discovery in the existing configuration core, preserving typed validation and test-profile compatibility.

user_story.narrative: As a developer, I want repository configuration to override shared user defaults so that I can reuse preferences without copying every setting into each repository.

acs.text: Configuration precedence is built-in defaults, selected user config, repository config, then personal project overrides; higher layers replace conflicting scalar/list values and recursively merge tables while retaining lower-layer keys omitted above, including explicit false and zero values.

User config selects the first existing file from `~/.config/solid-coder/config.toml` then `~/.solid-coder/config.toml`; repository config at each applicable directory selects `.solid-coder/config.toml` then `.config/solid.coder/config.toml`. If both aliases exist, only the first contributes settings.

A request from a nested directory preserves repository-root-to-request-directory overrides: each directory's selected repository config is followed by its `.solid-coder/config.local.toml`, with deeper directories overriding ancestors; user defaults are merged only once below this entire chain.

Missing optional files contribute no settings; a selected unreadable, malformed, or schema-invalid file reports its path and reason without silently selecting the lower-priority alias. The final merged settings receive existing typed validation, and omitted values receive built-in defaults without overwriting supplied lower-layer values.

With no user config, existing project settings and explicit test-model-profile selection retain their behavior; a clean CI home with committed project configuration produces the required project settings without a developer's home files.

input_output.input: Existing TOML settings schema, effective working directory, Git root marker, optional user/repository/local config files, and review/search targets from configuration or invocation.
input_output.output: A validated settings snapshot returned through the existing loading boundary to each requesting consumer for that operation, plus canonical repository-contained targets returned to review/search execution. No process-wide settings cache or mutable snapshot sharing is introduced.

technical_requirements.text: The configuration core owns root discovery, candidate selection, and precedence.
Start with the effective working directory: explicit request, existing project-directory environment setting, then process directory.
Resolve it and walk ancestors until the nearest Git marker; never merge project files from above that boundary.
Reuse the existing recursive table merge and typed decoder.
Apply user defaults once, then each directory's repository/local pair in root-to-leaf order.
An absent key uses the schema default only after all layers have merged.
Read settings anew at the existing operation boundary; no new cross-operation cache is required.
Candidate selection uses existence before parsing.
An existing preferred alias that cannot be read or parsed is an error, not permission to try the second alias.
Report the source file for invalid supplied settings; after merging, validate the complete settings contract and report merged-setting errors with their contributing sources.
Preserve the explicit test-model-profile override used by the existing test infrastructure.

Document that external setup can synchronize `.solid-coder/config.toml` as the canonical project location, that `.config/solid.coder/config.toml` is the exact supported alternate, and that mise may manage the primary user config.
Automation code outside this repository is a separate delivery.
Keep required CI configuration committed; optional personal files cannot be its sole source.

candidate_subtasks.title: Repository contained target execution
candidate_subtasks.description: Apply repository containment to every configured and explicit review/search target. Consume the root discovered by configuration and prevent content reads or dispatch when any target escapes.

user_story.narrative: As a developer, I want every review/search target interpreted within the selected repository so that shared defaults cannot cause another directory to be read as project source.

acs.text: The selected repository is the nearest ancestor Git root of the effective working directory, accepting both `.git` directories and worktree marker files; explicit working directory precedes the existing project-directory environment setting and process working directory. A review/search request without such a root fails before traversal.

Relative review/search targets from any config layer or invocation resolve against that repository root, including requests made from nested working directories; absolute paths within that root are accepted and targets are never anchored at the user config directory or home directory.

Outside-root absolute paths, parent traversal that resolves outside the root, and symlink escapes fail before target content is read, naming the offending target. Review/search enumeration excludes outside-root resolved entries even when reached through a directory or glob inside the root.

Legacy healthcheck and workflow review/search enforce the same boundary on configured and explicitly supplied targets; a rejected target prevents dispatch of that operation rather than silently broadening or dropping its requested scope.

input_output.input: Existing TOML settings schema, effective working directory, Git root marker, optional user/repository/local config files, and review/search targets from configuration or invocation.
input_output.output: A validated settings snapshot returned through the existing loading boundary to each requesting consumer for that operation, plus canonical repository-contained targets returned to review/search execution. No process-wide settings cache or mutable snapshot sharing is introduced.

technical_requirements.text: The review/search execution boundary owns target containment.
Resolve requested target paths and symlinks against the discovered root, compare by path components rather than string prefixes, and reject escapes before opening target content.
For target patterns, validate their literal anchor and validate each resolved match before reading it; discovered escapes produce the same target error rather than being followed.
An operation with any invalid target fails as a whole.
Existing nonexistent-target behavior remains unchanged after containment checks.
This is a boundary for project-source traversal, not a new security sandbox against concurrent filesystem mutation.
